description: Sea ice freeboard is the height of the sea ice surface above the local sea level. It is a critical parameter for estimating sea ice thickness using the principle of hydrostatic equilibrium. Freeboard can be measured by satellite altimeters (laser or radar) by comparing the ice surface elevation to the elevation of nearby leads (cracks in the ice exposing open water). For Antarctic sea ice, freeboard measurements are complicated by snow loading, which can push thin ice below sea level (negative freeboard), and by the presence of flooded ice layers. Accurate freeboard retrieval requires distinguishing between ice and water surfaces and establishing a reliable local sea surface reference. Freeboard is essential for calculating ice thickness, volume, and mass balance in polar regions.
title: Sea Ice Freeboard
